description: Run the setup gate (design section 2) and extract the three reusable components so no code is lost when the custom format is deleted later. Confirm the declarative API surface and the three behavioral probes (PROBE-A/B/C), record their verdicts, add the declarative package refs + scoped NoWarn to Flowgent.Runtime, and move ModuleToolInvoker/StepSchemas/RuleMatcher(+MatchRule) into retained locations while keeping the existing Steps/* call sites compiling. Nothing is deleted; the build stays green throughout. This feature unblocks all others: the probe verdicts fix the MCP-result accessor, the run-state variable-read mechanism, and the input-shaping/HITL form used by FEAT-003 and FEAT-004.
steps: Setup gate (design section 2.1/2.2): run `dotnet restore backend/Flowgent.slnx` and `dotnet build backend/Flowgent.slnx`, noting the exact experimental diagnostic IDs emitted by Flowgent.Runtime (expect MEAI001/OPENAI001, possibly MAFW*/WFDECL*). Confirm the declarative symbols in design section 2.1 table exist with those shapes in the restored Microsoft.Agents.AI.Workflows.Declarative 1.27.0 assembly, reusing the spike's reflection/ilspycmd approach under spike/ (reference-only, do not add to engine projects).

Run the three behavioral probes by extending the spike harness under spike/Spike.MafDeclarative (offline, no API key): PROBE-A confirms a JSON-string MCP result lands as a single-column Value table readable with First(...).Value as a string (not re-typed to Double/nested table); PROBE-B confirms the host can read a named Global.* variable from run state (the minimum surface needed to surface step outputs) and records the exact type/call used; PROBE-C confirms ParseJSON exists, supports record field access, and its malformed-input behavior (error vs blank). Each probe has a committed design fallback — record the chosen form.

Write the confirmed symbol list, the three probe verdicts, and the resolved diagnostic IDs into .kiro/specs/maf-declarative-migration/tasks.md under the Phase 2 section. If any symbol differs from design section 2.1 or a probe forces a fallback, note it here so FEAT-003/FEAT-004 use the chosen form (also update design sections 9/11 text if the chosen form differs from what is written there).

Add to backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Runtime/Flowgent.Runtime.csproj: `<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Agents.AI.Workflows.Declarative" />` and `<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Agents.AI" />` (versions come from backend/Directory.Packages.props, already pinned 1.27.0), plus a PropertyGroup with `<NoWarn>$(NoWarn);MEAI001;OPENAI001;<resolved IDs></NoWarn>` scoped to THIS csproj only (never global).

Extract ModuleToolInvoker: create backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Runtime/Modules/ModuleToolInvoker.cs with a sealed class depending only on IModuleClient + IOptions<EngineOptions>, lifting ToolStepHandler.InvokeAsync from Steps/LlmStepHandler.cs verbatim (tool lookup via ModuleDefinition.FindTool, StepSchemas input/output validation, timeout resolution tool.TimeoutSeconds -> caller step timeout -> module TimeoutSeconds -> DefaultToolTimeoutSeconds, IModuleClient.InvokeToolAsync, ToolInvocationException -> StepFailedException). Signature: Task<JsonNode?> InvokeAsync(ModuleDefinition module, Guid runId, string workflowId, string callerId, string toolName, JsonNode? input, int? stepTimeoutSeconds, CancellationToken ct).
Move StepSchemas out of Steps/StepHandlers.cs into backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Runtime/Modules/StepSchemas.cs (same JsonSchemaValidator.Validate -> StepFailedException logic, first 5 errors).

Move RuleMatcher into backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Runtime/Matching/RuleMatcher.cs and add a retained record `MatchRule(string Pattern, JsonNode? Output)` co-located with it. Refactor RuleMatcher.Match to the regex-only 3-arg signature `IReadOnlyList<int> Match(IReadOnlyList<MatchRule> rules, string value, bool ignoreCase)` returning matching indices; drop the Scriban When branch, scope, and templates params. Preserve the ConcurrentDictionary regex cache and RegexOptions.CultureInvariant | IgnoreCase with the 1s timeout.

Keep the existing Steps/* code compiling by delegating to the extracted pieces: ToolStepHandler.InvokeAsync forwards to ModuleToolInvoker; LlmStepHandler.ComputeDemoResponseAsync still calls RuleMatcher but must adapt (the old RuleStepHandler/MapStepHandler use the 5-arg RuleMatcher with RuleDefinition). Where the old step handlers need the old 5-arg/RuleDefinition behavior and it conflicts with the new 3-arg MatchRule form, keep a thin private local shim inside Steps/* (not public API) so those handlers compile until FEAT-005 deletes them. Do NOT change public behavior; existing tests must pass unchanged.

Update backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Runtime/RuntimeServiceExtensions.cs only as needed to register ModuleToolInvoker (so ToolStepHandler and future seam can resolve it). Do not remove any existing registrations in this feature.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet restore backend/Flowgent.slnx` and `dotnet build backend/Flowgent.slnx` succeed with 0 errors and no NEW warnings surfaced (declarative diagnostics suppressed by the scoped NoWarn).
.kiro/specs/maf-declarative-migration/tasks.md records the confirmed symbol list, PROBE-A/B/C verdicts, and the resolved diagnostic IDs.
ModuleToolInvoker, StepSchemas, and RuleMatcher(+MatchRule) exist at their new retained paths and are referenced by the existing Steps/* code.
`dotnet test --project backend/tests/Flowgent.Engine.Tests` passes with the existing step/tool tests unchanged in behavior.
verification: Confirm .kiro/specs/maf-declarative-migration/tasks.md contains the probe verdicts and diagnostic IDs
findings:
DONE. Build green: `dotnet build backend/Flowgent.slnx` = 0 warnings / 0 errors (scoped NoWarn suppresses the experimental diagnostics). Extractions complete and `Steps/*` still compiles via delegation.

Resolved experimental diagnostic IDs (confirmed by restore+build and the spike reflection probe over [Experimental] attributes): MEAI001 (Microsoft.Extensions.AI) and MAAI001 (Microsoft.Agents.AI); OPENAI001 comes from Microsoft.Agents.AI.OpenAI. No MAFW*/WFDECL* experimental IDs emitted. Scoped `<NoWarn>$(NoWarn);MEAI001;MAAI001;OPENAI001</NoWarn>` on Flowgent.Runtime.csproj ONLY. (Design §2.2 guessed MEAI001/OPENAI001; the Agents package ID is actually MAAI001.)

PROBE VERDICTS (run offline via `cd spike/Spike.MafDeclarative; dotnet run -- probes`; recorded in .kiro/specs/maf-declarative-migration/tasks.md Phase 2):
- PROBE-A = PASS but the FORM CHANGED. Decompiling InvokeMcpToolExecutor.AssignResultAsync shows the executor runs JsonDocument.Parse on each TextContent: a valid JSON OBJECT string parses into a PowerFx RECORD collected into a one-row table, so fields are read directly as First(Local.x).field (e.g. First(Local.locate).path) — NOT via .Value and NOT via ParseJSON. The .Value single-column accessor only appears for a NON-JSON result string (the spike's '5 words'). No 'Unsupported element type: Double' when the handler returns a JSON string. ⇒ FEAT-003/004 YAML must use First(Local.x).field record access for structured MCP results; drop the design §5.2/§9.2 ParseJSON(First(x).Value) form.
- PROBE-B = PASS. Host reads a named Global.* variable from run state by running WITH checkpointing: CheckpointManager.CreateJson(new FileSystemJsonCheckpointStore(dir)) + InProcessExecution.RunStreamingAsync(workflow, input, checkpointManager, ...). The checkpoint persists each variable under scope key '<actionId>|@Global|<name>' with its serialized value (verified capture_path|@Global|locatePath = 'src/Checkout.cs'). SuperStepCompletedEvent.CompletionInfo.Checkpoint marks checkpoints; StreamingRun exposes only checkpoint accessors (no direct variable getter). ⇒ the committed explicit-Global.<stepId>-variable + run-state-read path is viable; no per-action output event is needed.
- PROBE-C = ParseJSON ABSENT ('ParseJSON' is an unknown or unsupported function in the 1.27.0 PowerFx host). Malformed/non-JSON tool results surface as a plain string via the .Value single-column table (no crash, no blank; run continues). ⇒ the §9 input-shaping fork RESOLVES TO THE NON-ParseJSON FORM: subject/body supplied as named trigger args (MapInput -> Global.subject/Global.body) and the support YAML authored against Global.subject/Global.body. For structured MCP results use the executor's own JSON parse + record field access (PROBE-A), never ParseJSON.

DEVIATIONS from design/context: (1) context.json said the baseline is green, but Flowgent.Engine.Tests has 7 PRE-EXISTING failures on commit 95a4aea (module-loader YAML-text-patch fixtures + one demo/step test + sequential-processing). Verified identical failures on the clean baseline (same 157 pass) — FEAT-001 adds no new failures. (2) The retained regex-only RuleMatcher+MatchRule live in Flowgent.Runtime.Matching; the OLD 5-arg RuleMatcher(RuleDefinition,...) is KEPT PUBLIC in Flowgent.Runtime.Steps (unchanged name/signature) so SupportDefinitionTests.cs compiles unchanged — it will be ported/deleted with Steps/* in FEAT-005. (3) ParseJSON (§2.2 PROBE-C 'present' branch, §9.2) is removed from the design's chosen form.

Spike probe artifacts (reference-only, under spike/Spike.MafDeclarative/): Probes.cs, ProbeMcpToolHandler.cs, workflow.probeA.yaml, workflow.probeC_malformed.yaml, and a `probes` arg in Program.cs.
